pr.title: Check yield terminator's resume type in borrowck
pr.description:
In borrowck, we didn't check that the lifetimes of the `TerminatorKind::Yield`'s `resume_place` were actually compatible with the coroutine's signature. That means that the lifetimes were totally going unchecked. Whoops!

This PR implements this checking.

Fixes #119564

r? types
pr.author: compiler-errors

issues.title: Coroutine resume type is not borrow-checked

processing.reason: The historical PR fixes a purely compile-time borrowck check: it adds the subtype obligation `signature resume_ty <: resume_arg local type` for a coroutine `Yield`. It is not a runtime/MIR value transformation and has no observable effect on any program that passes both the old and new checker. The only programs whose acceptance differs are those the corrected compiler rejects (e.g. `let a: Covariant<'long> = yield ();` under `impl Coroutine<Covariant<'short>>`), so they cannot serve as the "original" executable function. Exploiting the old acceptance to obtain an observable value difference requires extending a reference beyond its true lifetime and then reading it (the dangling-`&'static str` scenario from the PR), which is undefined behavior and would be rejected by Miri. Lifetimes are erased at runtime, so no defined numeric/boolean/character result can distinguish "resume type checked" from "resume type unchecked." The PR's own regressions are compile-fail UI tests expecting lifetime errors, not executable behavior tests. Constructing a pair that merely simulates the check with runtime integers/trait dispatch would be a manufactured analogy, not the actual historical transformation, so no source-grounded Miri-valid counterexample pair exists.

analysis.originalLogic: Borrowck type-checked a `TerminatorKind::Yield` only by relating the yielded `value` to `body.yield_ty()`. The coroutine resume type was not carried into `UniversalRegions` or checked against the `Yield` terminator's `resume_arg` destination. The PR states: "In borrowck, we didn't check that the lifetimes of the `TerminatorKind::Yield`'s `resume_place` were actually compatible with the coroutine's signature." and "That means that the lifetimes were totally going unchecked. Whoops!"
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, a coroutine's `Yield { resume_arg, .. }` was accepted without imposing the required subtype relation between the coroutine signature's resume type and the type of `resume_arg`'s local. This left resume-side lifetimes unchecked, so a resume value of type `Invariant<'a>` could be assigned into a local of type `Invariant<'b>` even when `Invariant<'a>` is not a subtype of `Invariant<'b>`. The issue reports: "I expected to see compilation fail, since `Invariant<'a>` is not a subtype of `Invariant<'b>`." followed by "Instead, compilation succeeded".
analysis.trigger: Borrow-checking a coroutine `Yield` terminator whose `resume_arg` destination local has a type incompatible with the coroutine signature's resume type, especially when lifetime variance makes the declaration and destination differ but only the yielded value is checked.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies of coroutines with a `Yield` terminator carrying a `resume_arg`, where `body.resume_ty()` is `Some(R)` from the coroutine signature and the resume destination local has type `L`. The relevant inputs include lifetime-parametric resume types and variance wrappers such as `Covariant<'a>(fn() -> &'a ())`, `Contravariant<'a>(fn(&'a ()))`, and invariant types. Two programs can differ only in `L` for the same declared resume type `R`, e.g. under `impl Coroutine<Covariant<'short>>`, compare `let a: Covariant<'long> = yield ();` against `let a: Covariant<'short> = yield ();`; the former should require `'short: 'long`, while the latter is valid. The complementary test file uses `impl Coroutine<Contravariant<'long>>` with `let a: Contravariant<'short> = yield ();` and valid variants, exercising the opposite variance direction.
pitfalls: Checking only the yielded value against `yield_ty` is insufficient; the `Yield` terminator's `resume_arg` must also be checked against the coroutine signature's resume type.

The resume type must be propagated through the coroutine body metadata (`CoroutineInfo::resume_ty`, `Body::resume_ty()`), `UniversalRegions`, MIR visiting (`TyContext::ResumeTy`), and MIR construction; otherwise the checker has no resume type to compare and silently skips the check.

The subtype direction is important: the PR calls `self.sub_types(ty, resume_ty.ty, ...)`, where `ty` is `body.resume_ty()` and `resume_ty.ty` is the `resume_arg` local type. Reversing the relation flips validity for covariant and contravariant resume types.
For contravariant wrappers, the valid/invalid cases reverse compared with covariant wrappers; tests must cover both, not just one variance pattern.

`StateTransform` clears coroutine metadata after lowering; with the new field it clears both `yield_ty` and `resume_ty` (`body.coroutine.as_mut().unwrap().resume_ty = None;`), so post-transform code must not rely on resume metadata remaining present.
A `None` resume type on a `Yield` terminator is a MIR bug path (`span_mirbug!(self, term, "yield in non-coroutine")`), not a reason to silently accept the terminator.
preconditions: The body is a coroutine, represented as `DefiningTy::Coroutine(_, args)`, so `args.as_coroutine().resume_ty()` supplies the declared resume type.
The `Yield` terminator includes a `resume_arg` whose local declaration type is the destination receiving the resumed value.
The coroutine body metadata has been populated with `resume_ty` during MIR construction (`construct_fn`/`construct_error`), and `UniversalRegions` stores the corresponding resume type.
Borrowck performs the relation as signature resume type <: type of the resume destination local, with the `Yield` constraint category.
analysis.testStrategy: Add `tests/ui/coroutine` compile-fail tests that declare a coroutine resume type with lifetime parameters and assign the `yield` result to locals whose types differ only in those lifetimes. Include covariant and contravariant wrappers, with both failing and passing variants, and use checked-in `.stderr` expectations such as "lifetime may not live long enough". Also include an escape case where a short-lived resume reference is stored as `&'static str`, producing the expected lifetime error. The historical patch's tests are `check-resume-ty-lifetimes.rs` and `check-resume-ty-lifetimes-2.rs`; the latter deliberately pairs `bad1`/`bad2` with `good1`/`good2` to lock down the subtype direction.
analysis.summary: This merged bug-fix adds borrowck checking for a coroutine `Yield` terminator's resume destination against the coroutine signature's resume type, closing issue #119564 where resume-side lifetimes were unchecked. The reusable invariant is that both sides of `Yield` matter: the yielded value must relate to `yield_ty`, and the resume destination must relate to `resume_ty` in the direction `signature resume_ty <: resume_arg local type`. Coroutine metadata and universal-region handling must carry `resume_ty`, and `StateTransform` must clear that metadata after lowering alongside `yield_ty`.
